title: Acteoside alleviates blood-brain barrier damage induced by ischemic stroke through inhibiting microglia HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3 signaling.
authors: Liao, Yucheng; Hu, Junping; Guo, Chao; Wen, Aidong; Wen, Limei; Hou, Qiang; Weng, Yan; Wang, Jingwen; Ding, Yi; Yang, Jianhua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Acteoside通过抑制小胶质细胞HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3信号减轻缺血性脑卒中血脑屏障损伤，属于纯湿实验与临床前药理研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) can cause severe harm, inducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and pyroptotic death. IS treatment efficacy remains limited, and microglia are important regulators of IS-related blood-brain barrier (BBB) damage. It is thus vital that new therapeutic agents capable of targeting microglia be identified to treat IS-related damage to the BBB. Acteoside (ACT), which is a compound derived from Cistanche tubulosa (Schenk) Wight., offers promising bioactivity, but its ability to protect against central nervous system injury remains to be documented. To clarify the protective benefits and mechanisms through which ACT can protect against damage to the BBB, a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model system was herein employed. These in vivo analyses demonstrated that ACT was able to significantly reduce cerebral infarct size while improving their neurological scores and altering neurotrophic and inflammatory factor release. RNA sequencing and molecular docking studies highlighted the ability of ACT to exert its protective benefits via the HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3 axis. Western immunoblotting and immunofluorescent staining for tight junction proteins additionally confirmed the ability of ACT to preserve BBB integrity. The underlying mechanisms were then explored with an oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) model in vitro with BV2 cells. This strategy thus confirmed that the ability of ACT to suppress microglial inflammatory and pyroptotic activity was HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3 pathway-dependent. These data thus offer novel evidence that ACT can protect against IS-related damage to the BBB through the abrogation of inflammatory and pyroptotic activity, underscoring its promise as a novel lead compound for the therapeutic treatment of IS.
abstract_zh: 缺血性卒中（Ischemic stroke, IS）可造成严重损害，诱导氧化应激、炎症及焦亡性细胞死亡。IS的治疗效果仍有限，而小胶质细胞是IS相关血脑屏障（blood-brain barrier, BBB）损伤的重要调节因子。因此，识别能够靶向小胶质细胞的新治疗药物以治疗IS相关BBB损伤至关重要。毛蕊花糖苷（Acteoside, ACT）是从管花肉苁蓉（Cistanche tubulosa (Schenk) Wight.）中提取的化合物，具有前景良好的生物活性，但其对中枢神经系统损伤的保护作用尚待证实。为阐明ACT保护BBB损伤的益处及其机制，本研究采用大鼠大脑中动脉闭塞（middle cerebral artery occlusion, MCAO）模型系统。体内分析表明，ACT能显著减少脑梗死面积，同时改善神经功能评分，并改变神经营养因子和炎症因子的释放。RNA测序和分子对接研究突显了ACT通过HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3轴发挥其保护作用的能力。Western免疫印迹和免疫荧光染色对紧密连接蛋白的检测进一步证实了ACT维持BBB完整性的能力。随后，通过体外氧糖剥夺（oxygen-glucose deprivation, OGD）模型使用BV2细胞探讨了潜在机制。该策略因此证实，ACT抑制小胶质细胞炎症和焦亡活性的能力依赖于HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3通路。这些数据为ACT通过消除炎症和焦亡活性来保护IS相关BBB损伤提供了新证据，突显其作为IS治疗新型先导化合物的潜力。
